title: New York City plans to charge fee as containerization rollout expands
summary: The city’s Department of Sanitation is proposing to charge building owners up to $55 per unit in order to cover installation and maintenance costs. It’s also expanding use of the bins to more neighborhoods.

title: Waste and recycling bills left to watch as the 119th Congress wraps up
summary: Bills related to recycling initiatives for critical minerals have passed the House, but other recycling-related bills are still in committee. Notable sponsor Rep. Marianette Miller-Meeks, R-Iowa, lost her reelection.

title: Major waste companies spent $1.2B on Q3 M&A, driven by GFL
summary: WM and Republic Services also reported spending more year over year. Meanwhile, Waste Connections closed a deal for a family hauler in Oregon and Casella closed a deal for a Pennsylvania hauler.

title: PET recycling rate fell in 2025, but rPET content in bottles increased
summary: Lightweighting, imports and thermoforms are key factors that affected recycled PET markets, according to insights from NAPCOR, Dow Jones Energy, Advanced Polymer Recycling and Closed Loop Partners.

title: Casella aims to hit 26% margin by 2029, scraps NH landfill project
summary: Casella’s plan, a potential response to activist investor Jana Partners, included layoffs and operational updates in the mid-Atlantic. Casella also logged a $13.6 million write-off for abandoning a greenfield landfill plan.

title: Coalition forms to protect organic compost from packaging push
summary: The Safer Soils for All coalition, composed of the California Compost Coalition, WM, Republic Services, Recology and others, opposes a petition to USDA seeking to allow compostable products in organic agriculture.

title: EPA’s new PFAS strategy reveals focus on downstream cleanup
summary: The U.S. EPA’s newly announced strategy emphasizes technology partnerships for Superfund sites and downstream water contamination, even as the agency has been criticized for being slow to address upstream sources.

title: TRP’s new CEO strives for balance in policy and community projects
